contact._fields_readme: Only `message` has a placeholder. The test is whether it says something the label cannot: a sample company name is an example, not a format, and it silently picks a side on where 株式会社 goes in Japanese (this company puts it last). Name and email are fully described by their labels. A placeholder also disappears the moment someone starts typing, and whether it is announced varies by screen reader — it is not the place for a restatement of the label. `message` keeps one because "what should I write here" does not fit in a label.

works.heading: Selected work
works.lead: FarEdge Labs was incorporated on 29 July 2026, so what follows is the lead engineer's own record rather than the company's. The work was carried out under contract, on client sites or inside an employer — in every case for another company, which is why none of them can be named. Clients who agree to being named on the web will be named here from now on.

items.title: Machine learning models: training, quantisation and deployment
items.body: From model development through quantisation to running inside a real application. Feature design and data pipelines included.

items.title: Online sports simulation game — tech lead
items.body: Leading the development team across the whole stack, application through infrastructure. Moved to serverless: far stronger under concurrent load, at 60% lower operating cost.

items.title: Corporate site and internal cloud platform (this site)
items.body: A statically exported Next.js front end, a halftone renderer in WebGL / GLSL, and GCP serverless functions provisioned entirely with Terraform. Speak to the figure in the hero and a full-duplex voice conversation opens — the speaking model and the reasoning model are separate, and the function only relays one SDP offer, so no infrastructure of mine sits in the media path however long the call runs. Deployment authenticates through Workload Identity Federation, so there are no long-lived credentials anywhere.

items.title: Systems for a major automotive manufacturer
items.body: Full-stack work on driving analysis, a road information API and a health-data integration. One of the team that laid the infrastructure-as-code foundation, redesigning the AWS architecture from the build platform through to the application runtime, monitoring and alerting and a cross-account bulk data migration included. Proposals went to the product owner and the accepted ones I implemented. The always-on Tomcat / Java 8 stack was migrated in stages until no long-running instance was left, and the last step was settled by measurement — moving the implementation language from Java to Python more than halved the memory each invocation needed, and Lambda bills on memory × time.

items.title: Hotel support AI and automated check-in
items.body: A hashed URL emailed two days before arrival signs the guest in over JWT, so there is no account to create. Identity documents go through AppSync into S3 and guest details into DynamoDB, both encrypted with KMS, which satisfies the guest identification Japanese hotel law requires without staff in the loop — except the final match, which stays with a person. On the support side, a RAG and parallel-tool-calling agent answers enquiries and hands over the ones it cannot.

items.title: Edge AI inference benchmarking PoC
items.body: Testing whether an embedded AI accelerator's quoted performance holds up under a real workload. Handled INT8 quantisation (PTQ and QAT), ONNX conversion, inference and measurement — and answered the adoption question with measured numbers rather than the datasheet.

items.title: Internal operations system
items.body: Digitised time tracking, goal setting and payslips. Rather than standing up a new database, it used the Notion API to fit the operation the company already ran on. As tech lead: requirements, task breakdown, and allocating and tracking work across the team.

items.title: Cryptocurrency price prediction PoC
items.body: A multi-step Transformer forecast built in TensorFlow. Compared several feature configurations and dropped the news-derived features, which showed no measurable contribution.

items.title: Maintenance and feature work on a major metaverse platform
items.body: Proposed and led full automation of performance and load testing. Built the harness in FastAPI, automatic transfer of results to S3, and graphing and report generation from CloudWatch logs.

items.title: Agricultural field scoring PoC
items.body: Pulled Sentinel-2 NDVI and SAR data through Google Earth Engine and designed per-field scoring. Combined two observation types with different characteristics, so cloud-obscured optical data could be filled in.

items.title: Question answering AI for ophthalmologists
items.body: Embedded medical papers into a knowledge base and generated answers through vector search. An early BERT fine-tune was replaced with an external API — the binding constraint turned out to be latency and running cost, not accuracy.

items.title: Serverless CMS
items.body: React / Vite with AWS CDK. The project started on AppSync and moved off it — a GraphQL layer was heavier to run and more expensive to bill than this needed — leaving API Gateway calling Lambda, with everything resolved against DynamoDB and S3. CMS-equivalent features without depending on WordPress, handed over as a template that stays easy to edit.

items.title: Cloud migration and a production management platform
items.body: Moved a medical device manufacturer off on-premises infrastructure entirely. The file server went to AWS FSx, a production management system was built from scratch with role-based access control, and the entry point was redesigned around CloudFront, WAF and an ALB in a private subnet.

services.heading: Services
services.lead: Contract development. The five below are the usual shapes a request takes, and they combine freely. Why no client is named is explained on the work page.

offerings.title: Building something new
offerings.body: Requirements through to production release — front end, back end, runtime platform, CI/CD and security design, all of it.

offerings.title: Rearchitecting an existing system, and cutting what it costs
offerings.body: Revisiting architecture built around always-on servers. Usually that means moving toward serverless, without forcing anything that genuinely has to stay running. How much there is to save depends on the system, so the first thing delivered is a measurement and an estimate.

offerings.title: Getting machine learning into production
offerings.body: The strength is less in training a model than in landing one somewhere it actually runs: ONNX conversion, INT8 quantisation, feature design, and measured inference performance.

offerings.title: Technical validation and proofs of concept
offerings.body: Producing what you need in order to decide. Measured numbers from a real workload rather than a datasheet, shaped so the adoption question and the running-cost question can both be answered.

offerings.title: Making a codebase an agent can work in
offerings.body: Getting a codebase into a state where an agent can read it and be useful: conventions and documentation designed for that, and AI review wired into CI. The point is that your team can keep working the same way after handover.

offerings.title: Joining your team
offerings.body: Either holding one area as a member or leading the whole application as tech lead. Implementing tickets is not where it stops — design improvements get proposed actively, and when one is accepted the implementation comes with it.
